rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before Adam's creation, God announced to the angels that He would install him as a vicegerent on earth.
rows.anchor: إن الله تعالى قبل أن يخلق آدم عليه السلام قال للملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam was made from clay of divine might and from the light of Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وخلق آدم عليه السلام من طين العزة من نور محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God warned Adam that his commanding soul was his fiercest enemy and exposed its thoughts and desires to teach constant need and refuge: ask for aid in obedience, protection from sin, gratitude for blessing, and patience in affliction.
rows.anchor: وأعلمه أن نفسه الأمارة بالسوء أعدى عدو له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heart must not settle into even the slightest whisper of the lower soul; it must turn back to its Lord.
rows.anchor: ولا يساكن قلبه أدنى وسوسة لها دون الرجوع عنها إلى ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul is still when commanded and active at prohibition; Adam was to restrain its motion and move from stillness, with no escape from sin except God's protection and no obedience except by His aid.
rows.anchor: وجعل طبعها في الأمر ساكنا، وفي النهي متحركا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam was allowed to eat freely in Paradise but forbidden the tree; seeing it, he wished for permanence despite knowing his term was fixed, and Satan exploited that inward wish by promising the tree of immortality.
rows.anchor: فأتاه إبليس من قبل مساكنة قلبه بوسوسة نفسه في ذلك، فقال: هل أدلك على شجرة الخلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God allowed the enemy's whisper to reach Adam in accordance with prior knowledge, decree, and just judgment.
rows.anchor: وألحق الله عز وجل به وسوسة العدو لسابق علمه فيه، وبلوغ تقديره وحكمه العادل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following an unnamed Successor's twofold distinction of forgetfulness, Sahl reads Adam's as leaving the covenant; God left persistent sinners in punishment just as they had been left without His protection.
rows.anchor: يعني ترك العهد، ومثله في تنزيل السجدة

rows.speaker: بعض التابعين
rows.claim: The other sense is losing a memory, illustrated by Moses and the fish and Moses' request to al-Khidr; the Prophet is promised preservation from forgetting.
rows.anchor: والوجه الآخر النسيان هو الذي لا يحفظ فيذهب من ذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam's thought was an impulse of innate appetite, not reflective consideration; had it been contemplation, it would have become worship.
rows.anchor: ولم تكن فكرته اعتبارا، فكانت تكون عبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before creation God decreed that a heart settled on anything besides Him would face Satan's whisper through desire, while the person could instead return in refuge; Adam's deed became a lesson in his descendants through the Last Day.
rows.anchor: وهذا حكم الله تعالى به قبل خلق السماوات والأرض أنه لا يرى بقلبه عنده شيئا، وهو غيره مساكنا إياه، إلا سلط عليه إبليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eating was not the real point: God meant that Adam should not let his aspiration settle on anything other than Him.
rows.anchor: ولم يرد الله معاني الأكل في الحقيقة، وإنما أراد معاني مساكنة الهمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anyone who claims what is not theirs and settles inwardly on its desire risks divine abandonment, unless God mercies them by protecting them from self-management and aiding them against Satan and the ego.
rows.anchor: وكذلك من ادعى ما ليس له، وساكنه قلبه ناظرا إلى هوى نفسه فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise's people are protected from the self-management of worldly life; Adam was not protected from planning for permanence, so appetite and desire overpowered knowledge, reason, clarity, and the heart's light by prior decree.
rows.anchor: فأهل الجنة معصومون فيها من التدبير الذي كانوا به في دار الدنيا، فآدم صلوات الله عليه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet is quoted as saying that desire and appetite overcome knowledge and reason, explaining Adam's susceptibility to temptation.
rows.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels mean that they purify themselves by uttering what God graciously inspired them to say.
rows.anchor: أي نطهر أنفسنا بقولنا ما ألهمتنا تفضلا منك علينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṣāʿiqa means death, and more broadly any destructive punishment God sends upon whichever servants He wills.
rows.anchor: الصاعقة: الموت، والصاعقة: كل عذاب مهلك ينزله الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punished witnessed it directly, while God showed it to others as a lesson and warning.
rows.anchor: فينظرون إلى ذلك عيانا، ويريه غيرهم فيهم اعتبارا وتحذيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The 'good' left for testamentary bequests means lawful wealth.
rows.anchor: ما هذا الخير عندك؟ قال: المال الحلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading has Abraham wish to witness God giving life and death so that, when challenged, he could answer with certainty; direct witnessing reassures the heart.
rows.anchor: فيطمئن قلبي إلى الإجابة بنعم إذا شاهدت ذلك

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet is cited to affirm that direct witnessing is not like receiving a report.
rows.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading is that Abraham asked to see the dead restored to life as reassurance that God had taken him as an intimate friend.
rows.anchor: أنه سأله أن يريه إحياء الموتى طمأنينة له في أنه اتخذ خليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further reading makes this the elect's stance: asking God earns no claim on Him beyond what He makes real, and Abraham sought the revival of the dead to reassure his heart.
rows.anchor: أن سؤالي إياك لا أستحق به عليك إلا ما تحققه لي، وذلك موقف الخواص من خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Outwardly, the distant neighbor is a foreigner or stranger.
rows.anchor: أما ظاهرها فالجار الجنب: البعيد الأجنبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Outwardly, the companion by one's side is a travel companion.
rows.anchor: والصاحب بالجنب: هو الرفيق في السفر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternate reported outward interpretation identifies the companion by one's side as one's wife.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل الزوجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Outwardly, the wayfarer is a guest.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل الزوجة، وابن السبيل: الضيف، أما باطنها

words: وَٱلْجَارِ ذِى ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ وَٱلْجَارِ ٱلْجُنُبِ وَٱلصَّاحِبِ بِٱلْجَنۢبِ وَٱبْنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, the near neighbor is the heart, the distant neighbor the natural self, the companion reason following sacred law, and the wayfarer the limbs obedient to God.
rows.anchor: أما باطنها فالجار ذو القربى هو القلب، والجار الجنب هو الطبيعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They studied what the Scripture contained by abandoning the practice of it.
rows.anchor: ما فيه } [169] أي تركوا العمل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True remembrance is certain knowledge that God sees you, inward awareness of His nearness, modesty before Him, and choosing Him over yourself in every circumstance; merely claiming remembrance does not make one a rememberer.
rows.anchor: تحقيق العلم بأن الله تعالى مشاهدك

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In the saying that the world and its contents are accursed except God's remembrance, Sahl glosses remembrance as avoiding a forbidden act when one recalls that God is watching.
rows.anchor: قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sahl insists that anyone who spends even one breath outside remembrance is heedless of God.
rows.anchor: ما من أحد ذهب منه نفس واحد في غير ذكر الله إلا وهو غافل عن الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The elite's heedlessness is settling into a thing; the ordinary person's is taking pride in it.
rows.anchor: غفلة الخاص السكون إلى الشيء، وغفلة العام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What is more hidden than a secret is a thought the servant has not yet entertained, which comes to mind in sleep.
rows.anchor: أخفى من السر ما لم يفكره العبد فيه وهو مفكره نوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The staff first belonged to Adam, came from a Paradise myrtle, passed through the prophets to Shuʿayb, then Shuʿayb gave it to Moses with his daughter in marriage.
rows.anchor: أول من ملك العصا آدم، وهي من آس الجنة، ثم انتقلت من نبي إلى نبي

words: أَتَوَكَّؤُا۟ عَلَيْهَا وَأَهُشُّ بِهَا عَلَىٰ غَنَمِى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Besides leaning on it and shaking leaves for his sheep, Moses used the staff to gather fodder, fend off animals, make shade, guard him at night, light darkness, mark prayer time, and produce fruit when he was hungry.
rows.anchor: فكان موسى عليه السلام يتوكأ عليها، ويهش بها على غنمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God meant further benefits hidden from Moses, including its turning into a serpent and its striking rock and sea; this shows that even prophets' knowledge falls short of God's knowledge of events.
rows.anchor: فأراد الله تعالى مآرب ومنافع كانت خافية عليه، كانقلابها ثعبانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means not to tire the tongue with abundant remembrance while neglecting the heart's watchfulness.
rows.anchor: أي لا تكثر الذكر باللسان، وتغفل عن مراقبة القلب

words: فَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشْقَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following God's guidance means emulating the Prophet and keeping to the Book and Sunna, so one neither strays from guidance nor suffers in this life or the next.
rows.anchor: هو الاقتداء وملازمة الكتاب والسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God calls the inheritors His servants and marks them as righteous: only those wholly sincere for Him, who have made their inner life sound and cut themselves off from all besides Him, are fit for this inheritance.
rows.anchor: أضافهم إلى نفسه وحلاهم بحلية الصلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Outward humility is standing before God while observing the command's proper etiquette and purifying movement and stillness from all besides Him; its root is inward fear, which appears outwardly as humility and is a condition of faith.
rows.anchor: الخشوع علانية، وهو الوقوف بين يدي الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الحسن بن علي
rows.claim: Hasan ibn ʿAli's color changed after ablution; he explained that a person about to enter before the Lord of the Throne ought to change color.
rows.anchor: وقد حكي عن الحسن بن علي رضي الله عنه أنه إذا فرغ من وضوئه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet tells Muʿadh that the Qur'an restrains believers from many desires and ruin; they are bound to the truth, striving to free themselves and remaining anxious until they cross Hell's bridge.
rows.anchor: ويروى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال لمعاذ

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says believers know that watchers record their senses, limbs, and even small acts; piety accompanies them, the Qur'an guides, fear and longing lead, awe marks them, prayer shelters, fasting shields, charity frees, truth serves, modesty commands, and God watches.
rows.anchor: ويروى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال لمعاذ

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet tells Muʿadh that he loves for him what he loves for himself, conveyed what Gabriel conveyed, and hopes to find no one happier on Judgment Day for God's gifts.
rows.anchor: ويروى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال لمعاذ

words: يَخَافُونَ يَوْمًۭا تَتَقَلَّبُ فِيهِ ٱلْقُلُوبُ وَٱلْأَبْصَٰرُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day is the Resurrection, when hearts and eyes pass from state to state and find no lasting condition; believers fear it.
rows.anchor: يعني يوم البعث تتقلب فيه القلوب والأبصار حالا بعد حال لا يدومون على حال

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: When told that a man would emerge from Hell after a thousand years, al-Hasan wished that he himself might be that man.
rows.anchor: وقد حكي عن الحسن أنه قال: ذكر عنده أن رجلا يخرج من النار

words: يَخَافُونَ يَوْمًۭا تَتَقَلَّبُ فِيهِ ٱلْقُلُوبُ وَٱلْأَبْصَٰرُ
rows.speaker: عون بن عبد الله
rows.claim: ʿAwn ibn ʿAbd Allāh relates Luqman's counsel to hope in God without feeling secure from His plan and fear Him without despairing of mercy; the believer has one heart for hope and one for fear.
rows.anchor: حكي عن عون بن عبدالله أنه قال: أوصى لقمان ابنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God causes the speaker to die through heedlessness and revives him through remembrance.
rows.anchor: الذي يميتني بالغفلة ثم يحييني بالذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer asks God to grant Abraham praise among all peoples and assemblies.
rows.anchor: ارزقني الثناء في جميع الأمم والملأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking worldly goods out of desire deprives one of better things in this life and the next: the pleasure of worship and love of God here, and the highest ranks hereafter.
rows.anchor: من أخذ من الدنيا بشهوة منه حرمه الله في الدنيا والآخرة ما هو خير منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking what is needed because of personal compulsion or an obligation one must fulfill does not deprive one of what is better.
rows.anchor: ومن أخذ منها لضرورة دخلت بنفسه أو لحق لزمه لم يحرم ما هو خير في الدنيا

rows.speaker: عامر بن عبد قيس
rows.claim: When told he was content with little worldly provision, ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Qays said that one is even less content if one accepts the world as one's share of the hereafter.
rows.anchor: وقيل لعامر بن عبد قيس: لقد رضيت من الدنيا باليسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's 'remembrance' means remembrance and reflection.
rows.anchor: مبين } [69] قال: هو الذكر والتفكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah had been among those who fulfilled God's due before the affliction.
rows.anchor: يعني من القائمين بحقوق الله تعالى قبل البلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The false deity avoided here is worldly life: ignorance is its root, food and drink its branches, boasting its adornment, sins its fruit, and hardness and punishment its measure.
rows.anchor: الطاغوت الدنيا، وأصلها الجهل، وفرعها المآكل والمشارب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawaffī in the Qur'an has three senses: death, sleep, and being raised; at death God separates the luminous spirit's subtle self from the dense natural self that enables cognition and visions of the unseen.
rows.anchor: والتوفي في كتاب الله على ثلاثة أوجه: أحدها الموت، والآخر النوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In sleep, God withdraws the subtle self of dense nature but not the luminous spirit; the sleeper can awaken because that spirit remains, while its departure leaves a being without movement, dead.
rows.anchor: وإذا نام نزع عنه لطيف نفس الطبع الكثيف لا لطيف نفس الروح النوري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subtle natural self lives by the light of the spirit, while the spirit's own life is remembrance; the dead are called alive with their Lord because they are given remembrance through the luminous spirit.
rows.anchor: فحياة لطيف نفس الطبع بنور لطيف نفس الروح، وحياة روح لطيف نفس الروح بالذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dense nature lives through food, drink, and pleasure; a true knower reconciles nature and spirit so that both live by remembrance and striving in it.
rows.anchor: وحياة الطبع الكثيف بالأكل والشرب والتمتع، فمن لم يحسن الإصلاح بين هذين الضدين

rows.speaker: المبرد النحوي
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad the grammarian says spirit and soul are two connected things, neither of which can subsist without the other.
rows.anchor: وقال عمر بن واصل: وكان المبرد النحوي يقول: الروح والنفس شيئان متصلان

rows.speaker: سهل
rows.claim: Sahl rejects al-Mubarrad: spirit subsists in its own subtlety without dense nature, as God addressed the primordial beings with spirit, understanding, heart-perception, and subtle knowledge before bodily nature existed.
rows.anchor: فذكرت ذلك لسهل، فقال: أخطأ، إن الروح يقوم بلطفه في ذاته بغير نفس الطبع الكثيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By grace God leaves room for repentance until the final breath and accepts those who return then; Sahl calls this the clearest verse of divine compassion, since God brings His servants into generosity through His prior remembrance of them.
rows.anchor: أمهل الله تعالى عباده تفضلا منه إلى آخر نفس، فقال لهم

rows.speaker: جبريل
rows.claim: Gabriel tells Abraham that the generosity of God's pardon means He turns a forgiven sin into a good deed.
rows.anchor: وقد حكي عن جبريل عليه الصلاة والسلام أنه سمع إبراهيم عليه الصلاة والسلام يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sahl attests that his religion does not disavow sinful members of Muhammad's community, including killers, adulterers, and thieves, because God's special generosity toward this community cannot be fully measured.
rows.anchor: اشهدوا علي أني من ديني أن لا أتبرأ من فساق أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وفجارهم وقاتلهم وزانيهم وسارقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The regret is for being occupied with immediate worldly life, appetite, and the ego, and neglecting pursuit of God, reliance on Him, His rights, and constant service.
rows.anchor: اشتغلت بعاجل الدنيا ولذة الهوى ومتابعة النفس، وضيعت في جنب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prayer made with marwa is certainly answered; every believer's prayer is answered either in the exact request, without the person knowing, by averting harm, or by recording a good deed.
rows.anchor: الدعاء بالمروة مستجاب لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Supplication is called the best act because it is humble pleading and reliance that displays poverty and need.
rows.anchor: لأنه تضرع والتجاء وإظهار الفقر والفاقة

words: شَرَعَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلدِّينِ مَا وَصَّىٰ بِهِۦ نُوحًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah was the first to prohibit daughters, mothers, and sisters in marriage; God prescribed for this community the best aspects of the prophets' laws.
rows.anchor: فأول من حرم البنات والأمهات والأخوات نوح عليه السلام، فشرع الله لنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The charge given to Muhammad and the earlier prophets is to establish obedience to God and sincerity in it, and to manifest good character and spiritual states.
rows.anchor: من إقامة الطاعة لله وإقامة الإخلاص فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave prophets and some truthful saints awareness of His favors before they disappear and of His forbearance; anyone who recognizes blessings only in food, drink, and transport has belittled them.
rows.anchor: إن الله خص الأنبياء عليهم الصلاة والسلام وبعض الصديقين بمعرفة نعم الله تعالى عليهم قبل زوالها وحلم الله عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to turn away from them because he has exhausted his effort in conveying the message.
rows.anchor: أعرض عنهم فقد جهدت في الإبلاغ جهدك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God deadens the hearts of His enemies through disbelief and darkness, and gives His friends life through faith and the lights of gnosis.
rows.anchor: أمات قلوب الأعداء بالكفر والظلمة، وأحيا قلوب الأولياء بالإيمان وأنوار المعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the Qur'an easy for remembrance; without that ease, tongues could not bear to speak it, so people should take heed of this gift.
rows.anchor: هونا القرآن للذكر، ولولا ذلك لما أطاقت الألسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khaṣāṣa means hunger and poverty; Arabs call an impoverished person makhṣūṣ.
rows.anchor: تقول العرب: فلان مخصوص إذا كان فقيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of Medina prefer God's pleasure to their own desire, and their selflessness is evidence of love.
rows.anchor: فيؤثرون رضا الله على هواهم، والإيثار شاهد الحب

rows.speaker: وهيب بن الورد
rows.claim: Wahib ibn al-Ward transmits God's oath: one who prefers God's desire has worries reduced, affairs gathered, heart freed of poverty, and wealth before the eyes; one who prefers self accumulates worries, loses order and inner wealth, and is left to perish.
rows.anchor: وقد حكي عن وهيب بن الورد أنه قال: يقول الله تعالى

words: وَمَن يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفْسِهِۦ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being spared the soul's avarice means not clinging to anything besides God and His remembrance; such people abide with God in a good life.
rows.anchor: أي ومن يوق حرص نفسه وبخلها على شيء هو غير الله وغير ذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The 'unlettered' are those who affirm Muhammad and are ascribed to him because they follow and emulate him; one who does not emulate him is not of his community.
rows.anchor: الأميون هم الذين صدقوا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People are presented before God and judged for their deeds; nothing is hidden, all is recorded in prior knowledge, and they are asked about everything.
rows.anchor: أي تعرضون على الحق عز وجل، فيحاسبكم بأعمالكم، لا يخفى عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's questioning about favors includes whether one recognized the hours and gatherings granted for His sake and whether He answered a request for a wife; if He asks about such favors, how will He question about disobedience?
rows.anchor: ألم تكن عارفا بالساعات من أجلي؟ ألم يوسع لك حتى في المجالس

rows.speaker: عتبة الغلام
rows.claim: ʿUtba the ascetic says a believing servant may be held before God over a single sin for a hundred years.
rows.anchor: وقد حكي عن عتبة الغلام أنه قال: إن العبد المؤمن ليوقف

words: وَٱذْكُرِ ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ وَتَبَتَّلْ إِلَيْهِ تَبْتِيلًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Read 'In the name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful' at the opening of prayer: its blessing connects the worshipper to God and cuts them off from all else.
rows.anchor: اقرأ بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم في افتتاح صلاتك توصلك بركة قراءتها إلى ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-tarāqī refers to the throat.
rows.anchor: يعني الحلقوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inward reading, the earth is the heart: God splits it and grows there the blossoms of spirit, intellect, faith, and gnosis.
rows.anchor: وهو القلب { شقا } [26]، فأنبت فيها من ألوان الزهرة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet compares the Qur'an to a blossom in hearts, faith to rain planting richness, and greed to dew planting hypocrisy like grass.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " ألا إن القرآن زهرة في القلوب
